labels.label: bbsprop:classising
labels.notes: Unmarked (written `bbsprop:classising` without **), row partial: right. The causal clauses (l.537-545) are not stated, and the REPORT and the docstring both say so. What is stated is the link half, read on the paper's own definitions. (1) The type is not a choice. PairType reads l.862-922 on one oriented lifted developing pair (region of p, hyperbolic/parabolic holonomy with a fixed point, image of the developing map equal to i+/i-/(i- minus T)/a space-like arc, f = delta^k g with g hyperbolic/parabolic with a fixed point and the l.915 sign). HasType asks for some oriented pair. HasType.pairType carries it to every oriented pair, through IsLiftedDev.relate (f' = kappa f kappa^-1), angle_conj, conjugation invariance of hyperbolic/parabolic/fixed points, the chart-free characterisation of the degree-0 images by i+-(L) (deSitter_/bdPlus_/bdMinus_degree_zero_iff), and HSPositive's IsSpacelikePositive.forall for the sign. pairType_unique then excludes two readings of one pair by region, hyperbolic vs parabolic vs trivial holonomy, degree uniqueness (delta_zpow_mul_unique), image disjointness and sign clash. GammaLinkCircle.linkType is a choice only after existsUnique_hasType, so uniqueness is not true by construction. Requiring IsOrientedTangent is what makes the sign and the BTZ/cuspidal reading well defined. (2) The non-exhaustiveness finding is a faithful reading, not a strawman. l.794-795 assert that at p in dS^2 'L is a hyperbolic RP^1-circle', and l.797-800 the parabolic analogue. By l.690-694 a delta^k-quotient is an elliptic RP^1-circle (it 'includes the usual real projective structure on RP^1', whose holonomy delta is trivial in G). So a trivial-Gamma_p-holonomy circle at a non-time-like p is in no case of l.866-922: those cases need g hyperbolic (l.893-895) or parabolic (l.917-919). l.948-952 put no restriction on the circle (OQ-128 (a)). The witness, exists_isPositive_delta_four (HSPositive, unchanged), has lifted holonomy delta^4, is not IsRegular (not IsIso to the regular link), and has trivialHolonomy 4 as its only type. The finding restates OQ-128's finding at the level of the classification and does not contradict it. Its parenthetical 'k even' is not proved here; it is plausible, since odd delta-powers act as the antipodal map of l(p) (linkCover_add_one), which is not in Gamma_p. (3) Isomorphism: IsIso.hasType, linkType_eq and not_isIso_of_hasType are stated for same-p IsIso (OQ-120 (a)), which the docstring and the REPORT disclose. For circles at different points, not_isIso_of_hasType holds trivially, since IsIso forces C.pt = C'.pt. That is covered by 'moved-p isomorphisms not treated'. The Misner reading agrees with OQ-131. The lemmas say only that the type is an invariant; they do not say it is a complete invariant. Under moved-p isomorphisms Misner would split by chirality, which is SCOPE (c), and the converse (the type determines the circle) is disclosed as not formalized. The antipode table matches bbsrem:p_p: time-like and light-like future/past swap, space-like is kept, future cuspidal goes to past extreme BTZ-like. toLine is constant on {t, t.antipode} and sends cuspidal to extreme BTZ-like, as l.1011-1012 say. degree_even matches l.905, l.918 and l.1008. Existence is proved only for Misner and for space-like/light-like of degree 2k with both signs, and SCOPE (a) says so.

findings.what: Several colI_v1.tex line citations are off by 1-6 lines. The time-like item 'characterized by their cone angle, and by their future/past quality' is l.862-864, not l.856-858 (l.856-858 is the introduction to the enumeration). The extreme BTZ-like future case 'I = i^-' is l.887-888, not l.886 (l.886 is the cusp sentence). 'Recall that the degree is necessarily even' is l.1008, not l.1009. The causality restriction to degree 0 or 2 is l.1055-1056, not l.1059-1060 (l.1059 is the Misner CTC sentence).
